difficulty_reason: The retained unit is not solvable by assembling standard prerequisites. Its whole content is the passage of the Grothendieck-Serre and Nisnevich-type vanishing statements from a regular/Noetherian or Dedekind base to a SEMILOCAL PRÜFER base, and the classical tools do not survive that passage: Auslander's flatness criterion (the hinge of the classical proof) is a Noetherian statement, so the paper must construct a length function on finitely presented torsion modules over an essentially smooth local map from a valuation ring (Lemma 4.3, via a filtered-colimit and Henselian lifting argument) and re-run Auslander's induction in two cases (4.8, printed 213-216); purity for reflexive sheaves must be re-established over regular COHERENT rings (2.19, 2.21, 2.22); and the codimension bookkeeping must be done fibrewise over Spec R (3.2 with four labelled clauses, and 3.5, the Prüferian form of Česnavičius' Variant 3.7), which is exactly what forces the dimension-1 hypothesis in clause (ii). On top of that the proof needs the toral purity 7.9 and the toral Grothendieck-Serre 7.11, and a three-step curve replacement (8.5-8.7) that includes a reduction of Panin's finite-field trick to a counting inequality on residue-field points and a patching descent back to A^1_A. These are independent research-level constructions, not routine auxiliary steps. Two honest qualifications are recorded rather than hidden: (1) the paper's own proof of 8.1 is only three lines at native 2330-2332, because all the work is in 4.1, 2.19-2.22, 6.3, 7.9, 7.11 and 8.2-8.7, and a solver would have to reproduce that machinery; (2) the author states at 374-375 that clause (ii) generalises the main result of Ces22a to the Prüferian context and at 2136-2137 that clause (i) is a version of the Nisnevich conjecture inspired by Ces22b's Dedekind case, so the novelty is a generalisation of published theorems, not a statement nobody has proved in any form. Neither qualification reduces the difficulty: a generalisation whose base-class change invalidates the only known proof technique is research work, and the owner novelty decision for adoption purposes is recorded separately in NEXT_ACTION.json.
why_not_H2: H2 would be defensible only if the work consisted of applying Auslander's criterion, purity for reductive torsors and Grothendieck-Serre to a new class of rings. But none of those three can be applied: Auslander's criterion is stated for Noetherian rings and is re-proved here in a non-Noetherian form (4.1 via 4.3-4.8), purity for reductive torsors over regular local rings of dimension 2 (CTS79) is replaced by a fibrewise statement over a Prüfer base (6.3, 6.8, 6.9), and the Grothendieck-Serre conjecture is not known over Prüfer bases at all. The retained unit therefore requires new lemmas whose proofs occupy printed 210-216 and printed 227-234 rather than a citation.
why_not_H1: H1 is reserved for candidates whose difficulty is a routine exercise; nothing here qualifies, and the corpus admits only H2/H3 for new material.

non_routine_core_is_concrete.claim: the difficulty rests on named objects that the proof must build and control, not on the paper's length, its journal, its 128 citations, its 45 references or the fact that its TeX does not compile here

components.component: the length function l on finitely presented torsion A-modules supported on {m_A}, for an essentially smooth local map V -> A out of a valuation ring
components.why_non_routine: over a non-Noetherian valuation ring the torsion modules may all be zero, and the value group must be built from a totally ordered abelian group rather than from Z; the proof retracts to V when possible and otherwise passes to an absolutely integrally closed valuation ring V' and a faithfully flat A -> A'_(p), then pulls back. This is a construction, not a citation.

components.component: Auslander's flatness criterion over a valuation ring (Theorem 4.1), proved by a two-case induction on (r, d_x)
components.why_non_routine: the induction runs on the height r of the image point in Spec V together with d_x = dim O_{X_s,x}, uses the Ext-isomorphism lemma 4.5 and the two length estimates 4.8.1-4.8.4, and needs Claim 4.8.5 (Stacks 057F) to cut the dimension by one while keeping essential smoothness. The classical Noetherian proof gives no guidance at the steps where coherence replaces Noetherianity.

components.component: purity for reflexive sheaves over regular coherent rings and its consequences
components.why_non_routine: 2.19, 2.21 and 2.22 replace the usual depth-2 criterion by an intersection over the valuation-ring points of the scheme inside the generic stalk, with the equivalence (i)<=>(ii)<=>(iii) proved over locally coherent topologically locally Noetherian schemes; this is what later lets 6.8/6.9 run without Noetherian hypotheses.

components.component: the fibrewise codimension geometry over a Prüfer base (3.2) and the Prüferian geometric presentation (3.5, Česnavičius' Variant 3.7)
components.why_non_routine: 3.2 controls R-fibre dimension, generic-fibre dimension and codimension simultaneously through four labelled clauses; 3.5 produces an affine open U, an affine open S in A^{d-1}_R and a smooth R-morphism pi: U -> S of relative dimension 1 with Y ∩ U S-finite, which is the step whose validity the author says imposes dim R = 1 in 8.1(ii).

components.component: the toral purity 7.9 and the toral Grothendieck-Serre 7.11
components.where: native 2082-2089 and 2115-2133, printed 233-234, on the fppf local cohomology of 7.5-7.8 (printed 230-232)
components.why_non_routine: these replace the missing reductive-group inputs: 7.9 is a purity statement for H^0, H^1 and H^2 of a multiplicative-type group over a Prüfer base with codimension conditions, and 7.11 gives injectivity of the restriction maps to the function field in two scenarios, one of them via a compactification. Their proofs go through parafactorial pairs (7.4) and fppf local cohomology.

components.component: the three curve replacements 8.5-8.7, ending in the patching descent to A^1_A
components.why_non_routine: 8.5 equates the relative group with G_C after a finite etale neighbourhood, using the geometrically-unibranch case of 8.4; 8.6 needs a finite morphism etale at the points of Z-tilde and a counting inequality to avoid the finite-field obstruction to embedding Z into A^1_A; 8.7 patches a torsor across the complement of Z' using the surjectivity of two restriction maps and a gluing lemma. The final trivialisation then follows from the zero-section pullback being trivial by the section theorem of GL23.
